tickets.name: maestro update destroys user content in board/ — specs/ and reports/ wiped
tickets.desc:
DATA LOSS, reproducible. ai-maestro 0.1.22's new `maestro update` (commit 23f48e9) deleted 47 files from maestro/board/specs/, 7 from maestro/board/reports/, and overwrote maestro/board/README.md with the starter copy when run against lense-kit on 2026-08-08. Recovered here only because all 54 files were git-tracked; an untracked or uncommitted board would have lost them outright.

Cause — refreshVendoredKit() in ai-maestro/bin/cli.mjs:88-105. Its board/ branch removes every entry in the destination board/ that is not in BOARD_USER_FILES (cli.mjs:52 = {data.json, archive.json}) and does not exist upstream, on the assumption that 'not upstream means deleted upstream'. That inference is wrong for board/, which is a user workspace: specs/ and reports/ were never kit-owned, so they read as deleted-upstream and get rmSync'd. The vendored starter README the same run installed documents specs/ as a board folder — the kit knows it is user content; BOARD_USER_FILES does not.

Fix belongs upstream in ~/source/ai-maestro, which is HANDS-OFF from any lense-kit session (standing owner directive, same gate as T-004). This ticket carries the diagnosis, the repro, and the recommended patch; the owner lands it in an ai-maestro session. Adding 'specs' and 'reports' to BOARD_USER_FILES stops the bleeding but leaves the bad inference in place — prefer deriving the removal set from what the lock file previously recorded as vendored.

UNTIL FIXED: do not run `maestro update` in any repo whose board/ holds specs/ or reports/ — that is lense-kit and every separated product.

Companion spec: board/specs/T-001.md
tickets.note:
Filed 2026-08-08 after the incident. Working tree recovered via git checkout -- maestro/board/specs maestro/board/reports maestro/board/README.md. Vendored kit copy at maestro/{agents,bin,cockpit,docs,render,scripts,skills,starters,LICENSE,package.json,README.md,VERSION} + maestro/board/board.schema.json is now gitignored so it stops showing as untracked churn. Version skew to watch: .maestro.lock says 0.1.22, node_modules/@mychiefmind/ai-maestro is still 0.1.21, vendored copy is 0.1.22.

tickets.name: maestro-drift: detect hand-edits to generated files across all projects
tickets.desc:
The mechanism that keeps ai-maestro the source of truth AFTER separation. Because .claude/ must always be generated, any hand-edited file in it is a signal: someone improved something locally and never sent it upstream. Build a CLI that walks the registry (or the umbrella, pre-move) and reports per project: installed package version vs npm latest, and which generated files differ from a fresh render. Its output IS the promote-upstream worklist.

Independently shippable and useful BEFORE any project moves — it works against the current layout too. Pair it with a short CONTRIBUTING note describing the promotion ritual: generalize, strip project names/secrets/domains, file on the ai-maestro board, bump, publish.
tickets.note: Filed on the lense-kit board as kit-082; moved here 2026-08-08 — package work belongs on the package's board.

tickets.name: ai-maestro cockpit: portfolio mode — registry-aware multi-board console
tickets.desc:
Owner decision 2026-08-08: there is ONE board tool, and it is ai-maestro. Root cockpit/ is deleted (kit-099); everything it does that the package cannot must be upstreamed first. This ticket is that upstream.

Today maestro/cockpit/server/index.mjs:94-108 resolves exactly one BOARD_DIR and guards paths with isInsideKit — it structurally cannot show more than one project. Add a portfolio mode: given a registry file (the generic form of projects.json), serve N boards read-across, keep single-board mode as the default when no registry is present.

Capability gaps to close, measured against root cockpit (full diff: board/specs/T-003.md):
1. Registry read + allowlist — replaces cockpit/server/boards.mjs:26-59. The registry IS the write allowlist; the UI never supplies a path.
2. Multi-board read-across — /api/boards over N projects (root: boards.mjs readBoards()).
3. Survey / today — ready-ticket rollup across boards + isoWeek (root: boards.mjs survey():141, board half only; the marketing half goes to social-ops per kit-098).
4. Multi-root docs portal — root DocsPortal.tsx (296 LOC) lists docs across every registry project; package DocsPage.tsx (95 LOC) is single-root.
5. Report serving — /reports/:name (root index.mjs:185).
6. Stable service mode — root runs always-on at :3017 under launchd; package dev-scans from 4600. Needs a pinned-port service entrypoint so a launchd job can own it.

KEEP the package's existing hardening as portfolio mode is added: sanitize.mjs, the isInsideKit path guard, and the LOCAL_HOSTS header check (index.mjs:201-224) — root cockpit has none of these and must not drag its looseness upstream. Path containment generalises from 'inside the kit' to 'inside a registry-listed project root'.

ACs: (1) one cockpit instance serves every board named in a registry, read AND write, canonical-in-place with backups; (2) single-board mode unchanged when no registry is present; (3) path containment enforced against registry roots, no UI-supplied paths; (4) tests cover registry parsing, the allowlist rejection path, and multi-board read; (5) published to npm.

tickets.note:

tickets.name: toolkit/ vs package capability diff — upstream every generic gap
tickets.desc:
The umbrella toolkit/ injects per-project agent/skill/workflow overlays; ai-maestro ships a generic roster. Anything only toolkit/ can do is silent capability loss the moment a project switches. Diff toolkit/{agents,skills,workflows,templates} against the package and classify each item: generic (upstream to ai-maestro), project-specific (goes to that project's maestro/context.md), or dead. Upstream the generic ones as ai-maestro PRs.

Fold in the gaps already recorded in board/specs/kit-075.md §2 and §3: config-missing degrades silently (2a), agent-code aliasing is partial and undocumented (2b), --yes does not mean non-interactive (2c), setup ignores cwd (2d), and lense-kit has archive-only statuses Maestro lacks (§3).

This is the STATIC half. kit-086 (the speclense pilot) is the dynamic half — do both, because a real run finds what reading cannot.

tickets.name: Test suite deletes the repo's real board/specs/ on every run
tickets.desc:
DATA LOSS, reproducible, in the test suite itself. `npm test` removes the whole of this repo's `board/specs/` directory. Verified 2026-08-08 with a canary: wrote board/specs/CANARY.md + board/reports/CANARY.md, ran npm test, specs/ was gone and reports/ survived.

Cause — test/cockpit-server.test.mjs:75, in the after() hook:

    rmSync(join(SPECS, `${PROBE_ID}.md`), { force: true });
    try { if (existsSync(SPECS)) rmSync(SPECS, { recursive: true }); } catch { /* had other specs */ }

The intent is visible in the comment ("remove it and the dir if we made it") and in the catch ("had other specs"): the author expected rmSync to REFUSE a non-empty directory and to be caught. With { recursive: true } it never refuses — it deletes the directory and everything in it, including specs the test did not create.

FIX: delete only the probe file, then remove the directory only when it is empty and only when the test created it. Record whether SPECS existed in before(); in after() use rmdir (non-recursive) so a non-empty dir throws and is correctly swallowed, or readdirSync().length === 0 as the guard. Never rmSync(recursive) a directory the test does not own.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT from T-001: that one is refreshVendoredKit() in bin/cli.mjs deleting board/ entries missing upstream; this one is the test suite deleting the directory outright. Same invariant — board/ is user space, the kit is a guest in it — violated in two different files. T-001's own testCmd is `npm test`, so running that ticket's gate destroys that ticket's spec: land THIS first.

AC: a board/specs/ containing files the test did not write survives a full npm test run; a regression test asserts it.
tickets.note: Found 2026-08-08 while moving the package tickets onto this board: the three spec files written for T-001/T-003/T-004 vanished between writing them and `git add`. npm test was the only thing that ran in between. Regenerated from the lense-kit originals; they had never been committed, so nothing was recoverable from git — the same 'only survived because it was tracked' luck that T-001 documents did not apply here.
